examples.ko: 저는 서울 사람이 아니라 시골 촌사람이에요.
examples.en: I'm not a Seoul person, I'm a country person from a rural area.

examples.ko: 우리 부모님은 촌사람이라 서울이 아직 낯설어요.
examples.en: My parents are country folk, so Seoul still feels unfamiliar to them.

examples.ko: 처음 서울에 왔을 때 저는 완전 촌사람 같았어요.
examples.en: When I first came to Seoul, I felt like a complete country bumpkin.
You shouldn't tease a friend by calling them a country bumpkin.
They say that since long ago, country people have been generous.

examples.ko: 저는 촌사람이지만 서울 생활이 꽤 재미있어요.
examples.en: I'm a country person, but life in Seoul is quite fun.

explain: 시골에서 온 사람을 가리키지만, 놀리듯이 낮춰 말하는 느낌이 있을 때가 많아요. 본인이 농담처럼 쓰는 건 괜찮지만 다른 사람에게는 조심하는 게 좋아요. 중립적으로 말하고 싶으면 '시골 사람'이라고 하고, 반대로 '도시 사람'이라는 말이 있어요.
explain_en: It refers to someone from the countryside, but it often carries a teasing, slightly belittling tone. It's fine to joke about yourself, but be careful using it for others. For a neutral way to say it, use '시골 사람', and the opposite is '도시 사람'.

examples.ko: 촌수는 잘 모르지만 그분은 먼 친척 누나예요.
examples.en: I don't know our exact degree of kinship, but she's a distant relative, an older woman I call my older sister.
By degree of kinship, we're about eighth-degree relatives.
What is the degree of kinship between my maternal uncle and me?
When we worked out our kinship, we turned out to be sixth-degree relatives.

examples.ko: 촌수가 멀어서 얼굴도 거의 못 봤어요.
examples.en: We're distant relatives, so I've hardly ever seen their faces.

examples.ko: 친척 사이의 촌수를 헷갈리지 않게 표로 정리했어요.
examples.en: I organized a chart so I wouldn't mix up the kinship degrees among relatives.

explain: 친척 사이의 가깝고 먼 정도를 숫자로 세는 말이에요. 부모와 자식은 1촌, 형제는 2촌, 사촌은 4촌이라서 숫자가 클수록 멀어요. 보통 '촌수가 가깝다/멀다', '촌수를 따지다'로 말해요.
explain_en: It counts how close or distant relatives are using numbers. Parent and child are 1촌, siblings are 2촌, and cousins are 4촌, so a bigger number means a more distant relation. You usually say '촌수가 가깝다/멀다' or '촌수를 따지다'.

examples.en: Even though I'm wearing new clothes, I still look countrified.

examples.ko: 서울에 온 지 오래돼서 이제 촌티를 많이 벗었어요.
examples.en: I've been in Seoul a long time, so I've shaken off a lot of my country look.

examples.ko: 그 옷은 너무 촌티 나서 못 입겠어요.
examples.en: That outfit looks too frumpy and countrified, so I can't wear it.

examples.ko: 촌티 나는 말투를 고치고 싶어서 표준어를 연습해요.
examples.en: I want to fix my countrified way of speaking, so I practice standard Korean.

examples.ko: 촌티 내지 않으려고 옷을 새로 샀어요.
examples.en: I bought new clothes so that I wouldn't look like a country bumpkin.

examples.ko: 사투리 때문에 촌티가 난다고 걱정하지 마세요.
examples.en: Don't worry that your dialect makes you seem countrified.

explain: '세련되다'의 반대 느낌으로, 옷차림이나 말투가 시골스럽고 어색할 때 놀리듯이 써요. 보통 '촌티가 나다', '촌티를 벗다'로 말하고, 친하지 않은 사람에게 직접 쓰면 실례가 될 수 있어요. 형용사 '촌스럽다'도 같이 알아 두면 좋아요.
explain_en: It's the opposite of 'sophisticated' and is used, often teasingly, when clothes or speech look rural and awkward. You usually say '촌티가 나다' or '촌티를 벗다', and saying it directly to someone you aren't close with can be rude. It's also useful to know the adjective '촌스럽다'.

examples.en: You have to sew the stitches closely for the clothes to be sturdy.
Photos are packed closely together on the wall.

examples.ko: 이 일정표는 하루가 촘촘히 짜여 있어요.
examples.en: This schedule has every day packed tightly.

examples.ko: 모종을 촘촘히 심으면 잘 자라지 않아요.
examples.en: If you plant seedlings too close together, they don't grow well.
Stars are studded thickly across the night sky.

examples.ko: 그물을 촘촘히 짜서 작은 물고기도 잡혀요.
examples.en: The net is woven tightly, so even small fish get caught.

explain: 형용사 '촘촘하다'의 부사형이에요. 간격이 좁을 때뿐 아니라 일정이나 계획이 빈틈없이 짜여 있을 때도 써요. 반대로 간격이 넓고 드문 모양은 '듬성듬성'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It's the adverb form of the adjective '촘촘하다'. It's used not only for narrow gaps but also for schedules or plans that are packed with no free time. The opposite, with wide and sparse gaps, is '듬성듬성'.

examples.en: Candle wax dripped onto my hand and startled me.
I scraped the dripped wax off the table with a knife.
Candle wax hardens quickly once it cools.

examples.ko: 양초를 켜면 촛농 때문에 책상이 지저분해져요.
examples.en: When I light a candle, the desk gets messy because of the dripping wax.

examples.ko: 바닥에 떨어진 촛농도 같이 치워 주세요.
examples.en: Please clean up the wax that fell on the floor too.

examples.ko: 케이크 위로 촛농이 흐르지 않게 조심하세요.
examples.en: Be careful so the wax doesn't drip onto the cake.

explain: 촛불이 타면서 녹아 흘러내린 초를 말해요. 보통 '촛농이 떨어지다/흐르다/굳다'로 말하고, 양초 자체는 '초'나 '양초'라고 해요.
explain_en: It's the melted candle wax that runs down as the candle burns. You usually say '촛농이 떨어지다/흐르다/굳다', and the candle itself is '초' or '양초'.

en: candle stick; candle stand; candle holder

examples.en: I put a candlestick in the middle of the table.

examples.ko: 할머니 댁에는 오래된 놋쇠 촛대가 있어요.
examples.en: My grandmother's house has an old brass candlestick.
I stuck a candle in the holder and lit it.
This candle holder is made of glass, so it's pretty.

examples.ko: 촛대 위의 양초가 거의 다 탔어요.
examples.en: The candle on the holder has almost burned down.
I bought a candle holder too when I bought the candles.

explain: 초를 꽂아 세우는 받침이에요. 초 자체는 '초'나 '양초'라고 하고, 촛대는 그것을 꽂는 도구예요. 소리는 [초때]처럼 나요.
explain_en: It's the stand you put a candle in. The candle itself is '초' or '양초', and 촛대 is the holder for it. It's pronounced like [초때].

examples.en: Chonggak kimchi is made with small radishes, so it's crunchy.

examples.ko: 라면 먹을 때는 총각김치 하나면 충분해요.
examples.en: With ramyeon, a little chonggak kimchi is enough.

examples.ko: 엄마가 보내 주신 총각김치로 밥을 먹었어요.
examples.en: I ate rice with the chonggak kimchi my mom sent me.

examples.ko: 식당에서 총각김치도 좀 더 주실 수 있어요?
examples.en: Could you give me a bit more chonggak kimchi at the restaurant?
I helped make chonggak kimchi in the countryside.
The chonggak kimchi had turned sour, so I put it in a stew.

explain: 작은 무(알타리무)를 통째로 양념해서 담근 김치예요. 배추김치보다 아삭해서 라면이나 국밥 같은 음식과 잘 먹어요. 너무 시게 익으면 찌개나 볶음에 넣어 먹기도 해요.
explain_en: It's kimchi made by seasoning small whole radishes (알타리무). It's crunchier than napa cabbage kimchi, so people like it with ramyeon or soup with rice. When it gets too sour, it's often used in stews or stir-fries.

examples.en: In the second half, our team went on an all-out attack.

examples.ko: 게임에서 총공격이 시작되면 모두 앞으로 나가야 해요.
examples.en: When the all-out attack starts in the game, everyone has to move forward.

examples.ko: 상대 팀이 총공격으로 나와서 수비가 힘들었어요.
examples.en: The other team came at us with an all-out attack, so defending was hard.
The score was tied, so the coach ordered an all-out attack.
The last five minutes were an all-out attack, so even the goalkeeper went up.

examples.ko: 시험 전날 밤에 공부 총공격을 했더니 너무 피곤해요.
examples.en: I made an all-out study push the night before the exam, so I'm really tired.

explain: 모든 사람이 힘을 모아 한꺼번에 공격하는 거예요. 스포츠나 게임, 토론처럼 일상에서는 비유로도 자주 써요. 반대로 방어에 집중할 때는 '수비에 집중하다'라고 말해요.
explain_en: It means everyone joins forces to attack all at once. In daily life it's often used for sports, games, or figuratively, like a big push in studying. The opposite idea is focusing on defense, '수비에 집중하다'.

examples.en: I called the general affairs department and ordered office supplies.
I've been working in the general affairs department since last year.
Please ask the general affairs department about travel expenses.
A general affairs staff member booked the meeting room for me.
Company events are usually prepared by the general affairs department.

examples.ko: 총무부는 건물 관리와 비품 구매도 맡고 있어요.
examples.en: The general affairs department also handles building upkeep and buying supplies.

explain: 회사에서 사무용품, 건물 관리, 행사 준비처럼 여러 가지 살림을 맡는 부서예요. 회사에 따라 '경영지원팀'처럼 다른 이름으로 부르기도 해요. 월급을 다루는 곳은 보통 '인사부'나 '회계부'라서 구별해서 알아 두세요.
explain_en: It's the department in a company that handles many general tasks, like office supplies, building upkeep and event preparation. Some companies call it something else, such as '경영지원팀'. Pay and personnel matters usually go to '인사부' or '회계부', so keep them apart.

examples.en: This month's total revenue went up compared with last year.

examples.ko: 가게의 총수입에서 재료비를 빼면 순이익이 나와요.
examples.en: If you subtract ingredient costs from the shop's total revenue, you get the net profit.

examples.ko: 총수입은 많은데 남는 돈은 별로 없어요.
examples.en: The total income is high, but there isn't much money left over.
We combined the couple's total income and applied for a loan.

examples.ko: 광고 총수입도 내년에는 늘 거라고 예상해요.
examples.en: They expect total advertising revenue to grow next year too.
Half of my total income goes to rent.

explain: 비용을 빼기 전의 전체 수입을 말해요. 비용을 뺀 남은 돈은 '순이익'이라고 해요. 월급에서 세금 등을 빼고 실제로 받는 돈은 '실수령액'이라고 해서 구별해요.
explain_en: It's all the income before costs are subtracted. What remains after subtracting costs is '순이익' (net profit). The amount of salary you actually receive after taxes and so on is '실수령액', so keep them separate.

examples.en: Korea's total population is about 50 million.

examples.ko: 이 도시의 총인구가 해마다 줄고 있어요.
examples.en: This city's total population is shrinking every year.

examples.ko: 총인구 대비 노인 비율이 계속 높아져요.
examples.en: The proportion of older people compared with the total population keeps rising.

examples.ko: 지방 도시는 총인구도 줄고 청년도 줄었어요.
examples.en: In regional cities, both the total population and the number of young people have dropped.

examples.ko: 전체 총인구에서 학생이 차지하는 비율을 알려 주세요.
examples.en: Please tell me what share of the total population are students.
A report predicting the total population in 2050 has come out.

explain: 한 나라나 지역에 사는 사람 전체의 수를 말해요. 그냥 '인구'라고도 하지만, 총인구는 전체 합계를 강조해서 뉴스나 통계 자료에서 많이 나와요. 보통 '총인구 대비 ~%'처럼 비율과 함께 말해요.
explain_en: It refers to the number of all people living in a country or region. You can just say '인구', but 총인구 stresses the overall total and appears in news and statistics. It's often used with ratios, like '총인구 대비 ~%'.

examples.en: If you add up the scores for each item, you get the total score.
The total score for the exam is out of 100.
People with the higher total score get selected first.
Please calculate the total score of the two subjects.
Passing is decided by the total score.
I was five points short on the total score, so I failed.

explain: 여러 점수를 모두 더한 합계예요. 가능한 가장 높은 점수는 '만점'이라고 하니 총점과 헷갈리지 마세요. 점수를 사람 수나 과목 수로 나눈 값은 '평균'이에요.
explain_en: It's the sum of several scores. The highest possible score is '만점', so don't mix it up with 총점. The value divided by the number of people or subjects is '평균' (average).

examples.en: What is the maximum limit on the card?

examples.ko: 이 엘리베이터는 최대한도를 넘으면 소리가 나요.
examples.en: This elevator makes a sound if it goes over the maximum limit.

examples.ko: 집을 사려고 은행에서 최대한도까지 대출을 받았어요.
examples.en: I took out a loan up to the maximum limit from the bank to buy a house.
This is the most I can put up with.

examples.ko: 한 번에 보낼 수 있는 최대한도를 확인해 보세요.
examples.en: Please check the maximum amount you can send at one time.
I turned the phone volume up to the maximum.

explain: '최대한'은 '최대한 빨리'처럼 쓰는 부사이고, 최대한도는 '~까지', '~를 넘다'처럼 쓰는 명사예요. 반대말은 '최소한도'예요. 줄여서 그냥 '한도'라고 해도 돼요.
explain_en: '최대한' is an adverb used like '최대한 빨리', while 최대한도 is a noun used like '~까지' or '~를 넘다'. The opposite is '최소한도'. You can also shorten it to just '한도'.

examples.en: We adjusted the price to maximize profit.
I'm looking for a way to maximize the effect.
The room was small, so I maximized the space I used.
We need to maximize the strengths and reduce the weaknesses.

examples.ko: 운동 효과를 최대화하려면 꾸준히 해야 해요.
examples.en: To get the most out of exercise, you have to do it consistently.
That company maximized its earnings through advertising.

explain: '극대화하다'와 비슷하게 경영, 경제, 과학처럼 격식 있는 맥락에서 많이 나와요. 반대말은 '최소화하다'예요. 일상 대화에서는 '최대한 살리다'처럼 풀어서 말하기도 해요.
explain_en: Like '극대화하다', it appears mostly in formal contexts such as business, economics and science. The opposite is '최소화하다'. In casual talk, people often put it more simply, like '최대한 살리다'.

examples.en: There's an observation deck on the top floor of this building.
I took the elevator all the way up to the top floor.
I watched the night view from the top floor of the hotel.
Many companies use the top floor as their office.
In that apartment building, the top floor is the most expensive.
They say the top-floor unit gets hot in summer.

explain: 건물의 맨 위층을 말하고, 사회나 조직의 가장 높은 계층을 가리킬 때도 써요. 일상에서는 '맨 위층'이나 '꼭대기 층'이라고 쉽게 말하기도 해요. 반대말은 '최하층'이에요.
explain_en: It means the very top floor of a building, and it can also mean the highest class of a society or organization. In daily talk people also say '맨 위층' or '꼭대기 층'. The opposite is '최하층'.

examples.en: I went on a trip at the minimum cost.
It's okay to do this job at the bare minimum.

examples.ko: 다른 사람에게 최소한도 예의는 지켜 주세요.
examples.en: Please show others at least a minimum of courtesy.
I'll try to cut the cost down to the minimum.

examples.ko: 이 정도가 우리가 낼 수 있는 최소한도예요.
examples.en: This is the minimum we can pay.

examples.ko: 최소한도만 하자고 해서 일이 빨리 끝났어요.
examples.en: We agreed to do only the minimum, so the work finished quickly.

explain: '최소한'은 '최소한 이것만은 하세요'처럼 쓰는 부사이고, 최소한도는 '~까지', '~의'가 붙는 명사예요. 반대말은 '최대한도'예요. 보통 비용, 예의, 노력처럼 줄일 수 있는 것에 많이 써요.
explain_en: '최소한' is an adverb, as in '최소한 이것만은 하세요', while 최소한도 is a noun that takes '~까지' or '~의'. The opposite is '최대한도'. It's often used with things you can cut down, like cost, courtesy or effort.

examples.en: Try finding the minimum value in this graph.
Today's minimum temperature was five degrees below zero.
Please calculate what the minimum value is.

examples.ko: 최솟값보다 작은 수는 입력할 수 없어요.
examples.en: You can't enter a number smaller than the minimum value.
Find the difference between the minimum and maximum values.
I wrote code that finds the minimum value in an array.

explain: 반대말은 '최댓값'이고, 수학이나 통계, 프로그래밍 수업에서 많이 나와요. 맞춤법으로는 사이시옷을 넣어 '최솟값'으로 적어요. 일상에서는 '가장 작은 값'이라고 풀어 말하기도 해요.
explain_en: The opposite is '최댓값', and it appears often in math, statistics and programming classes. The standard spelling includes the sai-siot, '최솟값'. In everyday talk people may say '가장 작은 값' instead.

examples.ko: 우리 팀은 아직 최하위권에서 벗어나지 못했어요.
examples.en: Our team still hasn't gotten out of the bottom group.
My math grades were at the very bottom.

examples.ko: 한 경기를 지는 바람에 최하위권으로 떨어졌어요.
examples.en: We lost one game and dropped to the bottom group.
After working hard, I finally got out of the bottom group.

examples.ko: 최하위권 학생들을 위한 보충 수업이 열려요.
examples.en: A supplementary class is offered for students in the lowest group.
I'm not at the very bottom, but I'm not in the middle either.

explain: 순위가 맨 아래에 모여 있는 무리를 말해요. 맨 마지막 한 명이나 한 팀은 '꼴찌'라고 하고, 최하위권은 그 근처의 여러 명을 가리켜요. 반대말은 '최상위권'이에요.
explain_en: It refers to the group clustered at the very bottom of a ranking. The single last person or team is '꼴찌', while 최하위권 covers several near that spot. The opposite is '최상위권'.

examples.en: Does reading mystery novels improve your reasoning skills too?

examples.ko: 추리력을 키우려고 퍼즐 게임을 자주 해요.
examples.en: I play puzzle games often to build up my reasoning skills.
Is reasoning ability something you're born with?
It's a quiz that needs both reasoning and observation skills.

examples.ko: 추리력 때문에 친구들이 저를 탐정이라고 불러요.
examples.en: Because of my reasoning skills, my friends call me a detective.

examples.ko: 추리력이 뛰어난 사람은 작은 단서도 놓치지 않아요.
examples.en: People with great reasoning ability don't miss even small clues.

explain: 단서를 모아서 답을 알아내는 힘이에요. '관찰력', '판단력', '이해력'처럼 '-력'이 붙은 말과 같이 알아 두세요. 사람 마음을 알아채는 '눈치'와는 달라요.
explain_en: It's the ability to gather clues and work out the answer. Learn it together with other '-력' words like '관찰력', '판단력' and '이해력'. It's different from '눈치', which is about sensing what people feel.

en: pull oneself together; compose oneself; hitch up

examples.en: I'll pull myself together and try again.
I need time to get myself back in shape.
The shock was big, so it was hard to collect myself.

examples.ko: 아픈 몸을 추스르는 동안 집에서 쉬었어요.
examples.en: I rested at home while recovering from being sick.

examples.ko: 슬픔을 추스르면 다시 일할 수 있을 거예요.
examples.en: Once you get over the sadness, you'll be able to work again.
I hitched up my bag strap and climbed the stairs.

explain: '마음, 몸, 정신'과 함께 써서 흐트러진 상태를 다시 가다듬는다는 느낌이 있어요. '정신을 차리다'보다 천천히 회복하는 느낌이 있고, 흘러내린 짐이나 옷을 위로 올릴 때도 써요. '추슬러요', '추슬렀어요'처럼 '르' 불규칙이니 주의해요.
explain_en: Used with '마음', '몸' and '정신', it feels like straightening yourself out after things got disordered. Compared with '정신을 차리다', it suggests a slower recovery, and it also works for hitching up a slipping bag or clothing. It is a '르' irregular verb, so it becomes '추슬러요' and '추슬렀어요'.

examples.en: In autumn I keep thinking about chueotang.
I ate chueotang with perilla powder and sancho pepper added.
My father really likes chueotang.
How much is one bowl of chueotang?

examples.ko: 저는 추어탕은 아직 못 먹어 봤어요.
examples.en: I haven't tried chueotang yet.

examples.ko: 이 식당은 추어탕도 팔고 순댓국도 팔아요.
examples.en: This restaurant sells chueotang and also sundae soup.

explain: 미꾸라지를 넣고 끓인 진한 국이에요. 몸에 좋은 보양식으로 알려져 있고, 맛이나 재료 때문에 좋아하는 사람과 힘들어하는 사람이 나뉘어요. 먹을 때 들깻가루나 산초를 취향대로 넣어 먹어요.
explain_en: It's a thick soup made with loach. It's known as a nourishing health food, and people tend to either love it or find it hard because of the taste and ingredients. When eating, you add perilla powder or sancho pepper to taste.

en: letter of recommendation; letter of reference

examples.en: I asked my professor for the recommendation letter to submit to grad school.

examples.ko: 추천장 쓰는 데 시간이 오래 걸려요?
examples.en: Does writing a recommendation letter take a long time?

examples.ko: 선생님이 추천장에 제 장점을 자세히 써 주셨어요.
examples.en: My teacher described my strengths in detail in the recommendation letter.

examples.ko: 추천장은 다음 주 금요일까지 내야 해요.
examples.en: The recommendation letter has to be submitted by next Friday.
Please send the recommendation letter along with your résumé.
They say you can't apply without a recommendation letter.

explain: 입학이나 취업 때 다른 사람이 나를 소개하고 보증해 주는 글이에요. 한국에서는 '추천서'라고도 많이 말해요. 보통 '추천장을 쓰다/받다/내다'로 써요.
explain_en: It's a letter in which someone else vouches for you for admission or a job. In Korea people also say '추천서'. It's normally used as '추천장을 쓰다/받다/내다'.

examples.en: I pulled up my pants and started walking again.

examples.ko: 그는 눈썹을 추켜올리며 놀란 표정을 지었어요.
examples.en: He raised his eyebrows and looked surprised.

examples.ko: 무거운 가방을 어깨 위로 추켜올리는 모습이 힘들어 보였어요.
examples.en: Hitching the heavy bag up onto his shoulder looked tiring.
My skirt keeps slipping down, so I keep having to pull it up.

examples.ko: 안경을 코 위로 추켜올리면 잘 보여요.
examples.en: If I push my glasses up my nose, I can see well.
The jeans were too big, so I was busy pulling them up all the time.

explain: 바지, 양말, 안경, 눈썹, 어깨처럼 몸에 붙은 것을 위로 쭉 올릴 때 잘 써요. 반대로 아래로 내릴 때는 '내리다'를 써요. '추켜올려요', '추켜올렸어요'처럼 바뀌어서 어간이 달라지는 점에 주의해요.
explain_en: It's used when you pull something attached to the body upward, such as pants, socks, glasses, eyebrows or shoulders. For lowering something, you use '내리다'. Note that it changes form to '추켜올려요' and '추켜올렸어요', so the stem shape changes.

examples.ko: 청첩장을 받았는데 그날 다른 일정이 있어서 축의금만 보내려고요.
examples.en: I got a wedding invitation, but I have another plan that day, so I'm going to just send the gift money.

examples.ko: 친구 결혼식에 축의금을 얼마 내야 할지 고민이에요.
examples.en: I'm wondering how much gift money to give at my friend's wedding.
People usually put the gift money in an envelope.

examples.ko: 축의금 봉투에 이름을 쓰는 걸 깜빡했어요.
examples.en: I forgot to write my name on the gift money envelope.
I heard they went on their honeymoon with the gift money they received from friends.

examples.ko: 축의금이 부담돼서 결혼식에 안 가는 사람도 있어요.
examples.en: Some people skip weddings because the gift money is a burden.

explain: 결혼식에 가서 축하하는 마음으로 내는 돈이에요. 장례식에 내는 돈은 '부의금'이라고 하니 헷갈리지 마세요. 보통 '축의금을 내다', '축의금을 받다'로 말해요.
explain_en: It's the money you give at a wedding to show your congratulations. The money given at a funeral is called '부의금', so don't confuse the two. You usually say '축의금을 내다' or '축의금을 받다'.

examples.en: I got caught in the rain, and my clothes are soaked and damp.

examples.ko: 땀에 젖은 머리카락이 이마에 축축이 붙어 있어요.
examples.en: My sweaty hair is clinging damply to my forehead.
Tears dampened my cheeks.
I wet a towel well and wiped my face.
The ground is wet and damp, so be careful.
Dew has gathered damply on the blades of grass.

explain: '축축하다'의 부사형으로, 물기가 배어서 눅눅하게 젖은 모양을 말해요. '촉촉이'는 알맞게 부드럽게 젖은 좋은 느낌이 많고, 축축이는 불쾌하게 젖은 느낌에 자주 써요.
explain_en: It's the adverb of '축축하다', describing something soaked through and clammy. '촉촉이' often feels pleasant and gently moist, while 축축이 is often used for an unpleasantly damp feeling.

examples.en: There were over a hundred guests at the wedding.
I expressed thanks to the guests.

examples.ko: 개업식에 온 축하객을 위해 떡을 준비했어요.
examples.en: We prepared rice cakes for the well-wishers who came to the opening.

examples.ko: 축하객으로 온 친구들이 사진을 많이 찍어 줬어요.
examples.en: Friends who came to celebrate took lots of photos for me.
The guests applauded the bride and groom.
Many family members also came to celebrate at the graduation ceremony.

explain: 결혼식, 개업식, 졸업식 같은 행사에 와서 축하해 주는 손님이에요. 결혼식 손님은 줄여서 '하객'이라고도 해요. 장례식에서 위로하러 온 사람은 '조문객'이라고 불러요.
explain_en: It means a guest who comes to celebrate at an event like a wedding, shop opening or graduation. For weddings it's often shortened to '하객'. People who come to offer condolences at a funeral are called '조문객'.

examples.ko: 봄만 되면 춘곤증 때문에 낮에 졸려요.
examples.en: Every spring I get sleepy during the day because of spring fatigue.

examples.ko: 춘곤증이 와서 오후 내내 하품이 나요.
examples.en: Spring fatigue has hit me, and I yawn all afternoon.
They say light exercise is good for beating spring fatigue.
They say spring fatigue gradually gets better as the weather warms up.
I keep feeling tired lately, maybe because of spring fatigue.

examples.ko: 저는 춘곤증에 커피보다 산책이 도움이 돼요.
examples.en: For spring fatigue, a walk helps me more than coffee.

explain: 봄이 되면 나른하고 졸린 느낌이 드는 증상이에요. 봄 날씨 이야기에서 자주 나오는 말이에요. 점심 먹은 뒤에 졸린 것은 '식곤증'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It's the sluggish, sleepy feeling people get when spring arrives, and it comes up often in talk about spring weather. The sleepiness after lunch is called '식곤증'.

examples.ko: 춘분에는 낮과 밤의 길이가 거의 같아요.
examples.en: On the spring equinox, day and night are almost the same length.
This year the spring equinox is around March 20.
After the spring equinox, the days gradually get longer.
I looked for the spring equinox on the calendar.
They say farmers began preparing for farming around the spring equinox.
On the spring and autumn equinoxes, the sun rises due east.

explain: 24절기 중 하나로, 보통 3월 20일 전후예요. 낮과 밤의 길이가 거의 같고, 이후부터 낮이 길어져요. 짝이 되는 말은 가을의 '추분'이에요.
explain_en: It's one of the 24 solar terms, usually around March 20. Day and night are nearly equal, and the days get longer afterward. Its autumn counterpart is '추분'.

examples.en: Korea has four distinct seasons.

examples.ko: 춘하추동 중에서 어느 계절이 가장 좋아요?
examples.en: Out of spring, summer, fall and winter, which season do you like best?
This lake is beautiful in every season.

examples.ko: 춘하추동 열두 달 내내 일이 많았어요.
examples.en: I had lots of work all twelve months of the year.
I change my blankets to match each season.

examples.ko: 춘하추동마다 새 옷을 한 벌씩 샀어요.
examples.en: I bought one new outfit every season.

explain: 봄, 여름, 가을, 겨울을 한자어로 이어 부른 말이에요. 일상에서는 '봄여름가을겨울'이나 '사계절'이라고 말하는 경우가 있고, 춘하추동은 글이나 간판, 격식 있는 표현에서 볼 수 있어요.
explain_en: It's the Sino-Korean way of listing spring, summer, fall and winter in a row. In daily speech people may say '봄여름가을겨울' or '사계절', while 춘하추동 is seen in writing, signs and formal expressions.

examples.en: Please enter the departure point and the destination.
The flight departs from Incheon.
It takes two hours from the starting point to the destination.
I entered the wrong departure point in the taxi app.
Let's meet near the starting point and go together.
The departure point is Seoul and the destination is Busan.

explain: 반대말은 '도착지'예요. 내비게이션, 택시 앱, 여행 계획에서 자주 봐요. '출발점'은 시작하는 지점이나 시작 자체를 말할 때도 써서 조금 더 넓어요.
explain_en: The opposite is '도착지'. You often see it in navigation, taxi apps and travel plans. '출발점' is broader, as it can also mean the beginning of something.

examples.en: Korea's birthrate keeps falling.
A policy to raise the birthrate has been announced.

examples.ko: 지난해에 비해 출생률은 조금 올랐다는 기사를 봤어요.
examples.en: I saw an article saying the birthrate rose slightly compared with last year.

examples.ko: 출생률 하락이 사회 문제가 되고 있어요.
examples.en: The fall in the birthrate is becoming a social problem.
The population changes depending on the difference between the birthrate and the death rate.
We talked after watching the news about the birthrate.

explain: 태어나는 아이의 비율을 말하고, 반대로 사망하는 비율은 '사망률'이에요. 뉴스에서는 '저출생', '합계출산율' 같은 말도 같이 나와요.
explain_en: It refers to the rate at which babies are born, and the opposite rate of deaths is '사망률'. In the news, related terms such as '저출생' and '합계출산율' often appear alongside it.

examples.en: I filled in my date of birth and place of birth on my résumé.
My place of birth and where I live now are different.
My birthplace is the seaside city of Busan.
They asked me where my place of birth is.
I moved around a lot from my place of birth.
Relatives still live in the village where I was born.

explain: 태어난 곳을 말하고, 서류나 소개 글에서 주로 써요. '고향'은 자란 곳이나 마음의 고향까지 포함해서 출생지와 다를 수 있어요. 말로는 '어디에서 태어났어요?'라고 물어요.
explain_en: It means the place where you were born and is mainly used on forms and in introductions. '고향' can include where you grew up or feel at home, so it may differ from 출생지. In speech, you'd ask '어디에서 태어났어요?'.

examples.ko: 그 작가의 이름은 출판계에서 익히 알려져 있어요.
examples.en: That author's name is well known in the publishing world.
I often hear that the publishing industry is struggling.
People from the publishing world gathered at the book fair.
This year's talk of the publishing world is this novel.

examples.ko: 출판계는 요즘 전자책 시장에 관심이 많아요.
examples.en: The publishing world is very interested in the e-book market these days.
After graduating, I want to enter the publishing world.

explain: '-계'는 그 분야에서 일하는 사람들과 분위기 전체를 가리켜요. '연예계', '정치계', '체육계'도 같은 식이에요. 한 회사를 말하는 '출판사'와는 달리 업계 전체를 말해요.
explain_en: The suffix '-계' refers to all the people and the overall scene of a field, as in '연예계', '정치계' and '체육계'. Unlike '출판사', which is one company, 출판계 means the whole industry.

examples.en: I impulsively bought a plane ticket on the spot.

examples.ko: 충동적인 소비는 광고 때문에 생기는 경우가 많아요.
examples.en: Impulsive spending often happens because of advertising.

examples.ko: 제 동생은 충동적이라서 계획 없이 움직여요.
examples.en: My younger sibling is impulsive and moves without a plan.

examples.ko: 큰 결정은 충동적일 때 하지 마세요.
examples.en: Don't make big decisions when you're feeling impulsive.
I admit that the action was impulsive.

examples.ko: 충동적인 행동을 줄이려면 하루 정도 생각해 보세요.
examples.en: To cut down on impulsive behavior, try thinking it over for about a day.

explain: 생각 없이 그 순간의 감정이나 욕구로 움직일 때 써요. '충동적인 소비', '충동적으로 사다'처럼 '-인', '-으로'를 붙여 말해요. 반대 느낌은 '신중하다'나 '계획적'이고, 물건을 갑자기 사는 건 '충동구매'라고 해요.
explain_en: It describes acting on a momentary feeling or urge without thinking. It's used with '-인' or '-으로', as in '충동적인 소비' and '충동적으로 사다'. The opposite feel is '신중하다' or '계획적', and sudden shopping is called '충동구매'.
